penetration_assumption: The Rs 26,200 is ESTIMATED (the baseline below is VERIFIED). Anchor, not a demand model: an actually-stocked niche skincare SKU at ARY earns Rs 800-6,500/yr (VERIFIED per-selling-SKU: Lip Care Rs 1,324, Serum Rs 1,063, Face Pack Rs 786, Spf Rs 2,232, Glycerin Rs 2,158, Wipes Rs 2,927, Rose Water Rs 6,478). Line by line: (1) DIAPER-RASH CREAM Rs 3,100 — 322 diaper bill-lines in 12m implies ~22 infant households buying at ARY; assume half buy 2 tubes/yr at Rs 142. (2) HAND CREAM Rs 4,500 — ~150 canteen/housekeeping/laundry staff with hands in cold water; assume 20% buy one tube per winter at Rs 150. (3) CALAMINE Rs 6,000 — assume it takes 15% of the teen oil-control occasion already worth Rs 42,832 (Face Wash Gel line). (4) SPF LIP BALM Rs 2,400 — assume +15% on the existing Rs 15,883 Lip Care line. (5) KIDS/MINERAL SUNSCREEN Rs 2,200 — one SKU at the Spf line's observed per-SKU average. (6) BODY BUTTER Rs 4,000 — 2 SKUs, gifting only, at the niche per-SKU rate. (7) SYNDET CLEANSING BAR Rs 1,500 — the research itself says "stock 2-3 pieces, not a case". (8) TINTED LIP BALM Rs 2,500 — incremental only, since Maybelline Baby Lips already sells Rs 2,640. Generous upper bound if every line hits the top of the observed range: ~Rs 60,000. Margin: 25% assumed for this basket (above the category's 17.85% because these lines skew high — Lip Care 28.9%, Spf 30.4%, Face Pack 28.8%, all VERIFIED from the purchase ledger). This gap is 0.03% of ARY's turnover and 1.2% of its own skincare category.
probe_evidence: `ary assort probe` returned skus_matched = 0 (sold_12m 0, sales 0.00) for all five of: "hand cream"/"handcream"/"nivea hand"; "diaper rash"/"nappy"/"softsens"; "calamine"/"lacto calamine"; "body butter"/"mcaffeine"; "sun kids"/"la shield"/"kids sun". Wider SQL nets (8 patterns for hand cream, 6 for diaper rash, incl. sudocrem/desitin/barrier cream, aveeno/dove bar/soap-free, la shield/baby sun/mineral sun) confirmed each. Where a net did return rows they were all false: "%rash%" = Dr. Rashel face masks + "Crash Masala Candy"; "%lacto%" = Amul Lactose Free ice cream + Nestle Lactogen; "%shea%" = Nivea/W2 body LOTION; "%hand%" = Darshan Hand Bags, Harish Hand Towel, Tide "Lemon & Chandan". Zero real SKUs in all five. Also zero: syndet/soap-free cleansing BAR (Cetaphil LIQUID cleanser sells Rs 13,311+4,290+2,796, the bar format does not exist), SPF lip balm (only Vi-John "Li Guard", a plain balm, Rs 900), tinted lip crayon (1 dormant match). THE DIFF'S EVIDENCE WAS WORSE THAN ITS VERDICT — it called all 54 lines "covered" but 27 on broad matches, several of which are false coverage: heel/crack cream "covered, 86 SKUs, Rs 3.30 L on 'vaseline'" is really Medicare/Heel Repair = 3 SKUs, Rs 285/yr, all zero stock — the 62 heel/crack matches were Wheel detergent (Rs 1.18 L), Cadbury Dairy Milk Crackle, Haldiram Nut Cracker and Parle Krack Jack; body lotion "covered on 'winter'" matches Hemant/Navy Blue TRACK SUITS and woolen bed sheets; night cream on 'white', hand cream on 'coffee', tinted balm on 'candy', antifungal on 'ring', kids sunscreen on 'mineral', baby oil on 'dabur' are all noise. Its 57.8% coverage figure is unusable as stated, though the corrected answer still lands on "covered". CONVERSELY the research's own claim that barrier-repair cream is "what nobody stocks" is FALSE at ARY: Cetaphil Moisturising Cream 80g Rs 6,690, Moisturising Lotion 110ml Rs 9,300, Gentle Skin Cleanser 118ml Rs 13,311 all sell; sunscreen has 12 selling SKUs (Dot & Key, Pilgrim, Plix, Dermatouch) at Rs 26,778. Unlike dairy, ARY's Personal Care subgroup tree IS reliable for this category — a name-search of 34 skincare terms across all 93 groups found nothing material outside my 42-subgroup universe (the outside hits were ice cream, cream biscuits, soap case, scrubber, peanut butter).
top_skus: Himalaya Baby Diaper Rash Cream 50g (~Rs 142) — the only research must-have that is genuinely absent; zinc-oxide barrier cream is the one baby SKU parents will drive to town for
Lacto Calamine Oil Control 120ml (~Rs 180) — doubles as teen oil-control, which is why it outsells pure after-sun in India
Nivea Hand Cream 50-75ml (~Rs 150) — for canteen/housekeeping/laundry staff; needs a shelf-talker, nobody asks by name
Nivea Active Care SPF lip balm 4.8g (~Rs 160) — counter SKU through winter, sits beside the existing Eva/Himalaya balms
Cetaphil or Sebamed Cleansing Bar (2-3 pieces only) — the liquid cleanser already sells; only the bar format is missing
Himalaya/Mamaearth kids mineral sunscreen SPF 50 (1 SKU) — confirm with the school wardens' outdoor/sports calendar BEFORE buying
Plum or mCaffeine body butter 100-200g (2 SKUs) — gifting line only; Plum brand already has shelf presence at ARY
Lakme Lip Love or MARS tinted balm (2 SKUs) — marginal; Maybelline Baby Lips already covers this at Rs 2,640/yr
blockers: THE 8 ADDITIONS ARE NOT THE PRIORITY AND SHOULD NOT BE ACTIONED ALONE — 109 skincare SKUs that sold in Jun-Aug 2026 are at ZERO on-hand right now (VERIFIED), 3-month sales Rs 1,42,135 = Rs 5,68,540 annualised run-rate. That is 21.7x the entire assortment gap. Named live stockouts on proven sellers going into winter: Nivea Lotion 400ml (Rs 24,440/yr, 0 on hand), Vaseline Cocoa Glow 400ml (Rs 43,771/yr, 2 on hand), Clean & Clear Foaming 100ml (Rs 33,209/yr, 8 on hand).

RANGE, NOT SHELF, IS THE CONSTRAINT — assort/data/benchmark.json carries a sourced Skin Care sub-benchmark of 198 lines. ARY lists 1,447 active skincare SKUs and sells 498: 7.3x the benchmark line count listed, 2.5x it selling. Adding 12 SKUs against 949 dead codes worsens this. Any addition should be net of deletions.

THE 949 DORMANT SKUs ARE CATALOGUE DEBRIS, NOT UNSTOCKED DEMAND — 662 of 949 (70%) were NEVER purchased, not one line in the entire purchase ledger; 682 (72%) have NEVER sold in 1.1M bills; only 9 were purchased in the last 12m and only 9 have any stock. They are codes typed once (duplicate spellings like 'Ponds Cold Cream 55 Ml' / '55Ml' / '55 Ml Soft'). Revenue value of restocking them = Rs 0. The action is deletion.

LICENCE — allopathic antifungals (Candid/clotrimazole) are drugs under the Drugs & Cosmetics Act needing a Form 20/21 retail licence and a registered pharmacist. ARY already sells the OTC-permissible ones (Itch Guard, Ring Guard, Rs 3,145/yr combined). Do not extend this line; route to the campus dispensary.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH HP — every absent line is a low-velocity single. A distributor will not break a case for 2 pieces of Cetaphil bar. These go on a combined personal-care indent or not at all.

SUNSCREEN EXPIRY — 30-36 month shelf life with slow off-season rotation at a location where a case cannot be returned in a hurry. Negotiate near-expiry returns with the distributor before loading one.

SEASONALITY EVIDENCE IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS (my own first read was wrong) — skincare sales trough in Jan (Rs 80,783) and peak in Mar (Rs 2,81,492), which looks like the winter range going dark. Controlling for traffic kills most of it: the WHOLE SHOP halves in January (Rs 32.2 L vs Rs 95.1 L in May) because the residential campus empties for winter break. Skincare's share of shop holds at 2.0-3.6% all year. A winter lift in winter lines exists but is modest (0.50% of shop in Aug to 1.40% in Mar). I CANNOT separate 'not stocked in December' from 'nobody on campus in December' with this data — confidence on winter under-trading specifically is MEDIUM, not high.

MARGIN SOURCE — Rs 6,550 uses an assumed 25% for this basket. The category-wide 17.85% IS verified from PurchaseDetail.PurchaseCost vs SaleDetail (489 SKUs, Rs 19,42,509 net sales, Rs 15,95,754 COGS). Note the tax trap: PurchaseCost is ex-GST (IncludeInRate=false) while SaleRate is GST-inclusive (IncludeInRate=true) — comparing them raw gives a false 29.12%. Bath Soap, the volume line, runs at only 8.98%.
kill_reason: Not a kill, but close to one: the assortment gap is real yet trivially small, and the money is somewhere else. VERIFIED baseline, live 12-month window 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31, DB current to 2026-08-30 21:01 (the audit freeze is over): ARY's skincare universe is 1,447 active SKUs across 42 subgroups; 498 sold; gross Rs 22,55,977 (net of GST Rs 19,42,509) = 2.95% of ARY's Rs 7.65 Cr, Rs 480 per resident per year at 4,700 residents; gross margin 17.85% = Rs 3,46,755. Of the 54 researched SKU lines, 46 are COVERED by a substitute that actually sells — the top skincare SKUs are precisely the research's must-haves (Vaseline Skin Jelly 85g Rs 68,709; Himalaya Neem Face Wash 100ml Rs 49,663; Dove 100g Rs 47,953; Lux Fresh Glow Rs 39,835; Pears Rs 36,320; Clean & Clear Foaming Rs 33,209; Dettol Original Rs 32,704; Cinthol 4-pc Rs 25,545). 8 lines are genuinely absent (probe = 0 matches) and only ONE of those 8 (diaper-rash cream) is a research must-have; the rest are should-have or nice-to-have. Sizing them honestly against what a stocked niche SKU actually earns at ARY gives Rs 26,200/yr gross and Rs 6,550 of margin — 0.03% of turnover. Meanwhile 316 of the 498 selling SKUs (63%) are at zero on-hand; only 17 SKUs were available in all 12 months and those 17 alone did Rs 4,30,690 = 19% of the whole category; 110 SKUs sold in exactly one month of twelve. The 109 recently-selling, currently-empty SKUs alone carry a Rs 5,68,540 annualised run-rate — 21.7x the assortment gap. The central finding holds for skincare and is stronger here than the headline suggests, with one refinement: the 949 dormant SKUs are not 'listed but unstocked', they are 662 codes that were never once ordered. So the category has three actions in strict priority order — (1) reorder points and a September winter pre-book on the ~109 proven sellers now at zero, (2) delete the 662 never-purchased codes so the range stops lying about itself, (3) only then add the 8 lines above, on the next combined personal-care indent.
